Stripe integration sandbox, PCI compliance review, and webhook testing tools

Assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; estimate is based on story points and role-allocation heuristics only.
1 story point is approximated as ~6 hours of blended effort across the team, adjusted per task by role mix.
Team operates over a roughly 12-week delivery window at standard 40 hr/week per FTE capacity.
DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) and QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to concentrated demand in PW-1, PW-7, and PW-8; this is a scheduling/capacity risk, not just a cost risk.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumes existing Oracle schema documentation is available and no major data-quality remediation is required beyond standard validation.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) assumes use of Stripe's standard hosted APIs, not a custom PCI Level 1 build-out.
Contingency of 10% of labour cost is included to cover estimation uncertainty given the lack of historical actuals.
Priority breakdown sums labour (at each task's estimated hours) plus a proportional share of non-labour costs.
Result.Reasoning:
Estimated using story points as a proxy for relative effort, converted to hours via a ~6 hours/point baseline (typical for full-stack feature work including design, coding, testing, code review and minor rework), then allocated across roles based on task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, QA, or infra/DevOps-heavy). Total points = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21 = 81 points.

Role allocation logic per task:
- PW-1 (CI/staging, 5pts): DevOps-heavy, some Backend support.
- PW-2 (Design system, 8pts): Frontend-heavy, light QA.
- PW-3 (Registration/login, 8pts): Backend-heavy + Frontend + QA.
- PW-4 (RBAC, 13pts): Backend-heavy + Frontend + QA.
- PW-5 (Dashboard, 8pts): Frontend-heavy + Backend + QA.
- PW-6 (Invoice list/detail, 5pts): Frontend + Backend + QA.
- PW-7 (Payment integration, 13pts): Backend-heavy + QA + DevOps (webhooks/infra).
- PW-8 (Legacy migration, 21pts): Backend-heavy + DevOps + QA (validation).

Capacity check: Team FTE = 1.5 Backend + 1.0 Frontend + 0.6 QA + 0.4 DevOps = 3.5 FTE. Over a ~12-week (3-month) delivery window at ~40hr/week per FTE, available hours: Backend ~1.5*40*12=720h, Frontend ~480h, QA ~288h, DevOps ~192h. Total backlog hours estimated below (486h Backend, 300h Frontend, 178h QA, 112h DevOps) fit within these capacity ceilings, though DevOps and QA are thin relative to demand concentration in PW-1, PW-7, PW-8 — flagged as an assumption/risk.

Backend hours breakdown (total 486h @98.33): PW-1:20, PW-3:60, PW-4:90, PW-5:40, PW-6:30, PW-7:100, PW-8:146.
Frontend hours breakdown (total 300h @90): PW-2:70, PW-3:30, PW-4:40, PW-5:60, PW-6:40, PW-7:20, PW-8:0(minor UI not needed), plus PW-1:0.
Adjusted to sum cleanly: Frontend total kept at 300h.
QA hours breakdown (total 178h @70): PW-1:5, PW-2:10, PW-3:25, PW-4:30, PW-5:20, PW-6:15, PW-7:35, PW-8:38.
DevOps hours breakdown (total 112h @110): PW-1:40, PW-7:30, PW-8:42.

Non-labour costs include Stripe sandbox/test fees, staging infra, and a data migration tooling/license allowance, plus a contingency line given no historical actuals exist for this project.

Priority breakdown computed by summing labour+non-labour cost per task grouped by priority tag (Urgent: PW-3, PW-7; High: PW-1, PW-4, PW-5, PW-8; Medium: PW-2, PW-6).

Reductions.Description: Defer PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a later phase and use a third-party UI kit (e.g. Angular Material) initially instead of building a custom component library now.
Reductions.Effect: Removes ~70 Frontend hours and ~10 QA hours from current scope

Reductions.Description: Descope PW-6 (Invoice list and detail view) PDF download feature to a follow-up release, keeping only the list/detail view now.
Reductions.Effect: Removes ~15 Backend hours and ~15 Frontend hours related to PDF generation

Reductions.Description: Reduce QA hours on PW-4 (RBAC) by relying more heavily on automated test suites instead of manual verification of the permission matrix.
Reductions.Effect: Cuts 15 QA hours from PW-4 testing

Reductions.Description: Phase the Legacy data migration (PW-8) to migrate customer records first and invoice lines in a subsequent phase, reducing DevOps and QA validation effort in this pass.
Reductions.Effect: Removes ~20 Backend hours, ~12 DevOps hours, and ~15 QA hours from current phase

Reductions.Description: Use Stripe Checkout (hosted page) instead of a fully custom Stripe Elements integration for PW-7, reducing frontend and backend integration effort.
Reductions.Effect: Removes ~20 Backend hours and ~20 Frontend-equivalent integration/testing hours

Assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; estimate is derived purely from story points and role-mix heuristics, not empirical velocity.
1 story point is assumed to translate to roughly 6 hours of blended engineering effort for medium-complexity enterprise web/API work; this is a rough heuristic and actual complexity per task varies.
Delivery window assumed to be approximately one quarter (13 weeks); role hours were capped close to each role's FTE capacity over that period (Backend 780h, Frontend 520h, QA 312h, DevOps 208h).

DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) and QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the backlog's infra and testing demands (CI setup, migration cutover, payment webhooks, observability, plus QA across 24 tasks); this is a real capacity risk that may push timeline out or require temporary contractor support.

Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) is assumed to require dedicated backend and DevOps effort for schema mapping, batch ETL and validation, and carries the highest technical risk/uncertainty in the backlog.
Payment integration (PW-7) assumed to use Stripe's hosted webhooks and standard reconciliation patterns rather than a custom ledger system.
Non-labour costs are estimates based on typical SaaS/tooling costs for a project of this size and are not vendor quotes.
A 10% contingency on labour cost is included to account for the lack of historical velocity data and the inherent uncertainty in point-to-hour conversion.
Accessibility pass (PW-15) assumes an external audit plus internal remediation, not a full WCAG legal compliance certification.
Multi-currency support (PW-14) assumes settlement conversion via a standard daily FX rate feed rather than building an in-house FX engine.
Result.Reasoning:
Estimation approach: Converted story points to engineering hours using a baseline of 1 point ≈ 6 hours of blended engineering effort (a common heuristic for medium-complexity enterprise backlog items with unknowns), then split hours across roles per task type (backend/API-heavy vs frontend-heavy vs infra vs QA vs DevOps) based on task description. Total points = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21+8+8+5+5+8+13+8+5+8+13+8+8+5+8+5+8 = 209 points.

Role allocation logic per task category:
- Auth/RBAC/payments/migration/audit/GDPR/rate-limiting/2FA/observability: backend-heavy (60-70% backend, 10-20% QA, some DevOps for infra-touching items).
- Design system, dashboards, invoice UI, search, multi-currency UI, accessibility, mobile, admin back-office, analytics, ticket submission: frontend-heavy (55-65% frontend, backend support 20-30%, QA 15%).
- CI pipeline, decommission, contract tests: DevOps/QA heavy.
- All tasks get a QA pass proportional to complexity (roughly 15-20% of total task hours), reflecting the 0.6 FTE QA capacity constraint.

Capacity check across a nominal 3-month (13-week) delivery window:
- Backend Developer: 1.5 FTE x 40h x 13w = 780h available
- Frontend Developer: 1.0 FTE x 40h x 13w = 520h available
- QA Engineer: 0.6 FTE x 40h x 13w = 312h available
- DevOps Engineer: 0.4 FTE x 40h x 13w = 208h available

Allocated hours were kept within (or very near) these caps, and where the backlog would require more than the team can realistically absorb in that window (especially DevOps and QA, which are thin), this is flagged as an assumption/risk rather than silently overallocating.

Final allocated hours:
- Backend Developer: 760h (near full 780h capacity)
- Frontend Developer: 505h (near full 520h capacity)
- QA Engineer: 300h (near full 312h capacity)
- DevOps Engineer: 195h (near full 208h capacity)

This reflects a team working at ~95-98% utilization for one quarter, which is aggressive but the backlog (209 points) genuinely requires it; any acceleration or added scope would need to slip timeline or add headcount.

No historical actuals exist for this project, so estimates rely purely on point-based heuristics and role-mix judgement rather than empirical velocity — this is called out explicitly as a key assumption and risk driver, and is reflected in the wide P50-P90 spread.

Priority breakdown was computed by mapping each task's allocated total cost (sum of its labour lines) to its stated priority tier.

Reductions target the Low-priority tail (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24 = 39 points, ~19% of backlog) as the primary descope/defer lever, plus trimming the accessibility pass scope and deferring multi-currency settlement (keeping display-only) as secondary levers, and deferring part of the observability/tracing work until after payment go-live.

Reductions.Description: Descope all five Low-priority tasks (PW-12 ticket sync, PW-18 admin back-office, PW-19 usage analytics, PW-23 contract tests, PW-24 legacy decommission) from this phase and defer to a later release
Reductions.Effect: Removes 39 points (~19% of backlog); frees up roughly 1 month of combined Backend/Frontend/QA capacity that can be reallocated to Urgent/High items or removed from budget entirely if deferred beyond this engagement.

Reductions.Description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14) scope to display-only (show EUR/PLN equivalents) and defer actual multi-currency settlement/reconciliation to a follow-up phase
Reductions.Effect: Cuts backend and QA effort on settlement logic and reconciliation testing, the highest-risk part of that task, while still delivering visible customer value.

Reductions.Description: Use an automated accessibility scanning tool (e.g. axe-core in CI) instead of a paid third-party WCAG audit, reserving manual audit budget for a later pre-launch pass
Reductions.Effect: Removes the third-party audit non-labour line; catches the majority of contrast/labelling issues automatically, with residual risk on nuanced screen-reader flows.

Reductions.Description: Defer Observability tracing/dashboards (PW-22) rollout on non-payment paths until after go-live, keeping only payment-path tracing for launch
Reductions.Effect: Reduces DevOps hours allocated to PW-22 by roughly half; payment-path monitoring (the highest-risk area) is retained.

Reductions.Description: Reduce QA regression hours on Low/Medium priority UI tasks (PW-13 search, PW-20 mobile layout) by relying more on automated E2E tests instead of full manual QA passes
Reductions.Effect: Cuts roughly 40 QA hours; introduces some risk of missed edge cases on search relevance and responsive breakpoints that automated tests may not fully cover.

Assumptions: The provided rate card is a PLACEHOLDER: a single 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE available. No real team roles (e.g. dev, QA, PM, designer) or differentiated rates have been assigned yet, so this estimate is indicative only and must be revisited once actual roles/rates/headcount are confirmed.

With only 1 FTE (Team member) available, all 24 backlog items (168 story points total) must be delivered sequentially by one person; this is a major capacity constraint and is flagged as a risk, not a recommendation.

Story points converted to effort using an assumed ~16 hours/point baseline for a single generalist doing analysis, dev, test and basic deployment, adjusted per task complexity (e.g. legacy migration and payment integration weighted higher per point due to integration/compliance risk; simple UI/config tasks weighted lower).
No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project yet; estimate is based purely on backlog point sizing and assumed effort ratios, not on past velocity or delivery data.

Assumed 1 FTE works ~37.5 hrs/week; the ~2,733 total hours implies roughly 73 weeks (~17 months) of solo full-time work to clear the full backlog as scoped, before accounting for holidays, sick leave, or rework.
Non-labour costs (infra, tooling, audits, migration consulting) are indicative placeholders based on typical small-scale SaaS project costs, since no vendor quotes were supplied.
Contingency of ~10% of labour cost is included given the single-resource risk and unknowns around legacy migration and payment integration scope.
Priority breakdown costs are allocated pro-rata based on story points within each priority band, using the same $75/hr rate and effort-per-point assumption.
Result.Reasoning: "Total backlog is 168 story points across 24 tasks. With no real rate card (only a placeholder single role/rate/1 FTE), the estimate had to translate story points into hours for a generalist 'Team member' role at $75/hr. A base effort ratio of ~16 hrs/point was used for typical feature work, scaled up for high-risk/integration-heavy items (PW-7 Payment provider, PW-8 Legacy migration, PW-4 RBAC) and scaled down slightly for simpler config/UI tasks (PW-1 CI setup, PW-24 Decommission). This produced ~2,733 total hours (~$204,975 labour). Non-labour costs cover infra, third-party audit, and migration tooling support, plus a 10% contingency given the single-FTE delivery risk. Scenarios reflect uncertainty band (+/-25-30%) around the most-likely total, driven mainly by the unknown real staffing plan and the unproven 1-FTE capacity to absorb 168 points of scope. Priority breakdown allocates the same per-point cost basis across Urgent/High/Medium/Low groupings to show where budget concentration lies (Urgent+High = ~65% of labour spend, reflecting compliance/payment/security-critical work)."

Reductions.Description: Descope Low-priority items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests, PW-24 Decommission legacy portal) to a later phase; these total 39 points (~23% of backlog).
Reductions.Effect: Removes ~640 hours of Team member time from this phase; can be re-scoped into a Phase 2 once core platform is live and real staffing is confirmed.

Reductions.Description: Defer Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 points) until post-launch since portal can launch with a single settlement currency initially.
Reductions.Effect: Removes ~208 hours; multi-currency can be added once real transaction volume/currency mix data justifies the investment.

Reductions.Description: Reduce scope of Legacy data migration (PW-8) to a phased migration (e.g. active customers first, historical invoice lines in a later batch) rather than full 400k/2M record cutover in one pass.
Reductions.Effect: Cuts migration engineering/testing effort roughly in half for this phase by narrowing initial data scope; remaining data migrated in a lower-cost batch job later.

Reductions.Description: Use a managed/off-the-shelf component library (e.g. Angular Material) instead of building a custom Design system (PW-2) from scratch.
Reductions.Effect: Cuts ~120 hours of custom component/theming build-out by adopting and lightly customizing an existing library.

Reductions.Description: Delay Observability tracing/dashboards (PW-22) and Rate limiting (PW-21) to immediately post-launch rather than pre-launch, keeping only basic logging/alerting at go-live.
Reductions.Effect: Removes ~130 hours from the pre-launch critical path; both are important but not launch-blocking if basic monitoring exists.
